solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Funny performer in company, taking microphone briefly

indicators.note: the company takes on the next piece, so it is joined directly after

parts.note: mic is the short form of microphone

explanation.surface: A stand-up comedian in a touring troupe grabs the mike for a short spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A comedian or clown is a performer whose job is to be funny.

clue.text: Invitation from business leaders in Middle England

parts.note: CO, short for company, stands for a business

indicators.note: the leaders of the words Middle and England are their opening letters

explanation.surface: A firm's chiefs in the Midlands send out an invitation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Middle England' looks like a region, but only its two first letters, M and E, are used.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'Come!' to someone is an invitation to join you or approach.

clue.text: Impressionist painter trimmed long hair

indicators.note: trimming cuts the end off, so the painter's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Édouard Manet was a French Impressionist painter

explanation.surface: An Impressionist artist gets a haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trimmed' drops the final T of MANET.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse's or lion's mane is the long hair on its neck.

clue.text: Old Spanish writer shattered a TV screen

indicators.note: a shattered thing is broken into pieces, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone has smashed a television screen.
explanation.definitionFit: Miguel de Cervantes, author of Don Quixote, was a Spanish novelist of the 1500s.

clue.text: Type of vintage car: commander takes girl aboard

indicators.note: taking someone aboard puts them inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: CIC is short for commander-in-chief
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A naval commander welcomes a young woman onto the ship.
explanation.walkthrough: C-in-C, commander-in-chief, is written without hyphens here; 'takes' is only a link, and 'aboard' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A classic car is an older, collectable model, one sort of vintage motor.

clue.text: Conservative supporter recruiting millions with little fuss

parts.note: C abbreviates Conservative, the British political party

indicators.note: a supporter recruiting someone takes them in, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: an ally is a supporter

explanation.surface: A Tory backer quietly signs up millions of new members.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with little fuss means doing it in a composed, unflustered way.

clue.text: Wood imported into Tashkent

indicators.note: something imported into the city name sits inside it, so the answer is buried in its letters

explanation.surface: Timber is shipped into the capital of Uzbekistan.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash is a hardwood timber from the tree of the same name.

clue.text: Mates who run riot, to a certain extent

indicators.note: letters that run riot go wild and fall out of order

explanation.surface: Friends who go wild do so only up to a point.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean partly or rather, to a limited degree.

clue.text: Building material — cement, originally, on Greek island

indicators.note: the original letter of cement is its first one

parts.note: Crete is the largest Greek island

explanation.surface: Cement is being used, in the first place, on a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cement' looks like part of the definition but supplies only its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Concrete, a mix of cement, sand and gravel, is a basic construction material.

clue.text: Underground worker wants a large fizzy drink

parts.note: a miner works below ground
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A miner fancies a big bottle of pop.
explanation.walkthrough: In British use a mineral is a fizzy soft drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Minerals is an old British term for carbonated soft drinks.

clue.text: Smell an earthling

parts.note: in British slang a hum is a bad smell

explanation.surface: An order to sniff a person from Earth.
explanation.definitionFit: An earthling is a person, a member of our species, as aliens in fiction would say.

clue.text: Lonely female at dance makes a bloomer

definitions.meaning: a girl left without a partner at a dance, sitting by the side
a flowering garden plant with fragrant spring blooms

explanation.surface: A girl left alone at a dance commits a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' reads as a mistake, but here it is something that blooms, a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The plant name is also the term for a shy person without a dance partner, who stands against the wall.

clue.text: Communist supporters: revolutionary listens in

indicators.note: a revolutionary change turns things over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A revolutionary eavesdrops on a conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: Followers of Lenin's form of Marxism back his communist doctrine.

clue.text: Cocktail in US school prom?

parts.note: a high school is an American secondary school, giving its first word
a prom is a formal dance, a ball

explanation.surface: A cocktail served at an American school dance.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a high-school ball, the whole picture, also builds the drink's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A long drink of spirit with soda or ginger ale over ice is called by this name.

clue.text: Beating bridge champion?

parts.note: a span is a bridge or the arch of one
a king is the top figure, the champion, in a field

explanation.surface: Defeating the best bridge player in a card game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bridge champion' suggests the card game; here bridge is a structure across a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A spanking is a beating, a smacking given as punishment.

clue.text: One saying nothing about president's principal attribute

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the silent word goes about, around, the next letter

parts.note: someone mute is saying nothing

indicators.note: the principal letter of the word is its first

explanation.surface: A silent person wraps the head of state's main quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attribute' looks like a noun but is the verb, to ascribe.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascribe blame or a quality to someone is to credit it to them.

clue.text: Not entirely popular role

parts.note: something in fashion is said to be in
an actor's part is a role

explanation.surface: A role that is only partly well liked.
explanation.definitionFit: Partly, to some degree but not wholly, is the meaning of the phrase.

clue.text: More sober Greek holds party

indicators.note: the abbreviation holds the party within its two letters

parts.note: a rave is a big dance party

explanation.surface: A Greek man hosts a gathering, though he is the soberest one there.
explanation.definitionFit: Graver, the comparative of grave, means more serious and solemn.

clue.text: Gymnastic feat: offer some fresh water afterwards

indicators.note: the water comes after, so it follows the first piece

parts.note: to hand someone something is to offer it
a spring is a source of fresh water

explanation.surface: After a tumbling routine, the gymnast is handed spring water.
explanation.definitionFit: A handspring is a gymnastic move flipping over on the hands.

clue.text: Tamil uprising — leader goes missing in capital city

indicators.note: the leading letter of the name is dropped
in a down clue an uprising reads the word from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A Tamil revolt fails once its head is lost, in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' turns TAMIL into LIMAT; 'leader goes missing' drops the T, Tamil's leading letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Lima is the capital city of Peru.

clue.text: Criminal tendency

definitions.meaning: in slang, a crooked or dishonest person or police officer

explanation.surface: A tendency towards crime.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means crooked in slang and also an inclination, as in an artistic flair.

clue.text: Part of Birmingham is home for religious sect

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A district of Birmingham houses a religious group.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'for', which is a link word; the sect alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amish are a traditionalist Christian group, mostly in Pennsylvania.

clue.text: Feverish and throaty from time to time

indicators.note: taking letters only now and then means every other one

explanation.surface: A patient is running a temperature and has a croaky voice now and again.
explanation.definitionFit: Feverish means having a raised temperature, so feeling hot.

clue.text: Remnant of undergarment I get shortened

parts.note: a vest is a British undershirt worn under clothes

indicators.note: a shortened word loses its end letter

explanation.surface: A scrap is all that is left of my underwear after it shrank.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a vest is an undershirt, not a waistcoat.
explanation.definitionFit: A vestige is a trace or remnant of something that has mostly gone.

clue.text: Boat with less cargo?

definitions.meaning: a flat-bottomed barge used to unload ships
carrying a smaller load, so less heavy

explanation.surface: A boat carrying a smaller load.
explanation.definitionFit: The barge takes cargo off ships, leaving them less heavy; the comparative of light fits the second sense.

clue.text: Stylish forms of transport going into reverse

indicators.note: going into reverse means the word is read backwards

parts.note: trams are street vehicles that carry passengers

explanation.surface: Fashionable vehicles are backing up.
explanation.definitionFit: Smart describes clothes or people that are well dressed and fashionable.
